claims.says: Day 1: Drive to Cutthroat Lake trailhead or Rainy Pass. Hike to approach base (3-4 hours via Cutthroat Lake route, or 2-3 hours via PCT). Scout route and camp if needed. Day 2: Climb North Ridge - West Side
Be off technical terrain by 2:00 PM

contradictions.why: The trip plan is laid out as two days with a camp, while PUBLISHED TIMES and the turnaround describe a single 9-hour day with an alpine start.

contradictions.fact: Cutthroat Lake camp text describes a different peak's approach

claims.says: It does not serve Cutthroat Peak's south-side routes or the usual North Ridge approach: those start from a different trailhead, a long pullout on SR 20 about 1.5 miles west of Washington Pass
(1) From the Cutthroat Lake trailhead on Highway 20, hike 1.8 miles with 500 feet elevation gain to Cutthroat Lake (4,800 ft).

contradictions.why: On the Molar Tooth North Ridge page the camp says the 'usual North Ridge approach' starts from a pullout west of Washington Pass and is not served by Cutthroat Lake, but this route's own approach (1) goes via Cutthroat Lake; the text is about Cutthroat Peak.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The camp note is copied from Cutthroat Peak; approach, road and waypoints for this route never use the pullout west of the pass.

claims.says: Clear skies with 40-50°F overnight freezing for early-morning frozen gully conditions.
Alpine temperatures 55-75°F in July-August with overnight freezing common (40-50°F).

contradictions.why: The same sentence calls 40-50°F nights 'freezing', which they are not.

claims.says: Small unpaved parking lot at Rainy Pass trailhead.
Cutthroat Peak Climbers Trail Pullout (Hwy 20, ~1.5 mi W of Washington Pass, north side)
From the long pullout on the north side of SR-20 about a mile and a half west of Washington Pass

contradictions.why: ACCESS sends the party to a Rainy Pass trailhead lot while the trailhead card, waypoint and approach all start at the SR-20 pullout west of Washington Pass.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Waypoint, approach_logistics, approach, approach_variants and road.driveNote all use the SR-20 pullout; access.notes is the outlier.

contradictions.why: From a 4,947 ft trailhead to an 8,066 ft high point is at least ~3,120 ft of net gain (more with the drop to State Creek), not 2,500.

contradictions.internal_resolution: timing, itinerary and fitnessSpec agree on ~10 h+; the 8-hour figure is the outlier.

claims.says: Roughly 2-3 hours from the SR 20 pullout through meadows/the approach bowl to the ridge saddle

contradictions.fact: Whether the notch-gaining 5.7 pitch is one of the 8 pitches

claims.says: Gains the North Ridge Notch via loose, runout terrain
One loose, runout 5.7 pitch to the North Ridge Notch.
~8 pitches, mostly 2nd-4th class ramps and corners
THIS PITCH SHOULD BE TREATED AS THE TECHNICAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL CRUX OF THE APPROACH, NOT OF THE RIDGE ABOVE IT.

contradictions.why: ROUTE BREAKDOWN counts the notch pitch as P1 of 8, while the itinerary adds ~8 ridge pitches after it and the approach calls it part of the approach, implying 9.

contradictions.fact: Which line is the peak's classic

claims.says: Eight pitches at 5.7. This is the peak's classic line.

contradictions.internal_resolution: overview and crowds agree the South Buttress is the standard classic; the approach_variants sentence is the outlier.
